claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA replaces raw attention-mass ranking with a closed-form score that measures how much each sparse unit reduces matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: MASA uses matrix-product error reduction to rank sparse units instead of raw attention mass

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a theory-grounded plug-in correction, MASA can be added to existing sparse attention frameworks without changing their sparse kernels or budgets.
claims.claim_summary: MASA plugs into existing sparse attention frameworks without changing kernels or budgets

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Extensive experiments across multiple sparse attention methods, benchmarks, and LLM backbones show consistent accuracy gains, supporting both MASA and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: MASA achieves consistent accuracy gains across multiple sparse methods, benchmarks, and backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We propose Matrix Approximation Sparse Attention (MASA), a theory-grounded plug-in correction for sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: The paper introduces MASA as a plug-in correction for sparse attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA keeps the sparse units, kernels, and budgets of existing sparse attention methods, but replaces their raw attention-mass ranking with a closed-form score derived from matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: MASA replaces attention-mass ranking with a closed-form matrix approximation error score

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a result, MASA can be added to diverse sparse attention frameworks without changing their implementation interface.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into diverse sparse attention frameworks without altering implementation interfaces

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We identify a long-standing selection mismatch in sparse attention: existing magnitude-based rules approximate the attention matrix entrywise, while the Transformer uses attention through matrix multiplication.
claims.claim_summary: The paper identifies a selection mismatch between magnitude ranking and attention matrix multiplication

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We propose MASA, a theory-grounded plug-in scoring method that ranks sparse units by their closed-form reduction in matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: MASA ranks sparse units by closed-form matrix-product approximation error reduction

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA can be integrated into existing sparse attention baselines while keeping their sparse kernels and budgets unchanged.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into baselines while keeping sparse kernels and budgets unchanged

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under matched settings with the original baselines, MASA gives consistent accuracy gains, supporting both the proposed method and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: Under matched baseline settings, MASA consistently improves accuracy across evaluated configurations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA keeps their sparse unit definitions, sparse kernels, and budget rules unchanged, and only replaces the score used to rank candidate sparse units.
claims.claim_summary: MASA preserves baseline unit definitions, kernels, and budgets, replacing only ranking scores

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All MASA scores are computed at the same profile resolution as the baselines.
claims.claim_summary: MASA computes scores at the profile resolution of underlying baselines

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA therefore does not require a new full-resolution dense attention map beyond the information used for sparse-unit ranking.
claims.claim_summary: MASA avoids requiring a full-resolution dense attention map beyond baseline ranking data

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This computation only uses matrix products and score matrices at the profile resolution, without materializing the N × N × r contribution tensor.
claims.claim_summary: MASA's score computation operates at profile resolution without constructing high-dimensional tensors

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA improves all eight matched average scores across three sparse methods, three benchmark suites, and both Llama- and Qwen-family backbones.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves all eight matched average scores across evaluated methods, benchmarks, and backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On InfiniteBench, MASA raises FlexPrefill-Llama from 47.14 to 47.99 against a full-attention score of 48.06, recovering approximately 92% of the original average-score deficit.
claims.claim_summary: MASA recovers 92% of FlexPrefill-Llama's score deficit relative to full attention on InfiniteBench

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On RULER, MASA raises SeerAttention from 87.60 to 88.09, moving it from below the dense reference to above it.
claims.claim_summary: MASA boosts SeerAttention on RULER from 87.60 to 88.09, surpassing full attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, replacing the ranking score adds 0.76 points, exceeding the original method’s 0.48-point advantage over full attention and increasing that advantage to 1.24 points.
claims.claim_summary: MASA adds 0.76 points to FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, extending its lead over full attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Thus, MASA improves already strong sparse systems without increasing their sparse budgets or changing their kernels.
claims.claim_summary: MASA enhances sparse system performance without altering budgets or execution kernels

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the four RULER configurations at 32K, 64K, and 128K, MASA improves 11 of 12 matched length-level scores.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves 11 of 12 RULER evaluation scores at 32K, 64K, and 128K context lengths

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For every configuration, the mean gain over these longer contexts at 32K–128K exceeds that at 4K–16K.
claims.claim_summary: MASA's accuracy gains are larger at 32K–128K contexts than at 4K–16K contexts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 128K, MASA improves MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen by 1.28, 0.48, 1.45, and 2.16 points, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: At 128K length on RULER, MASA improves all four framework configurations by up to 2.16 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 64K, the gains reach 2.16 points for FlexPrefill-Llama and 3.65 points for FlexPrefill-Qwen.
claims.claim_summary: At 64K length on RULER, MASA improves FlexPrefill variants by 2.16 and 3.65 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On LongBench, MASA improves SeerAttention’s 8K+ score from 52.69 to 53.16.
claims.claim_summary: MASA increases SeerAttention's 8K+ context score on LongBench from 52.69 to 53.16

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The evaluated MASA configurations reduce normalized squared output error in all four framework–backbone pairs, providing direct empirical support for matrix-product preservation.
claims.claim_summary: MASA reduces normalized output approximation error across all evaluated framework-backbone pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen, replacing the original ranking score with MASA adds empirically negligible overhead relative to the sparse attention runtime and remains far below the dense attention cost.
claims.claim_summary: MASA introduces negligible computational overhead relative to baseline sparse runtime

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The overhead also stays negligible at 128K, the main regime where sparse attention is needed.
claims.claim_summary: MASA's runtime overhead remains negligible at 128K sequence length

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Therefore, MASA improves accuracy without weakening the practical efficiency of the underlying sparse attention method.
claims.claim_summary: MASA enhances model accuracy while preserving the runtime efficiency of sparse baselines

claims.claim_text_verbatim: First, raw MASA already improves the original sparse baseline in several settings, which supports the matrix-product scoring objective itself.
claims.claim_summary: Unadjusted raw MASA outperforms original sparse baselines across multiple benchmark settings

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Second, norm control can further improve the score in settings where value-norm outliers affect sparse-unit ranking.
claims.claim_summary: Norm control mechanisms further improve MASA scores by handling value-norm outliers

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Norm clipping is helpful for SeerAttention and FlexPrefill-Llama, while soft norm balancing is useful in some FlexPrefill settings.
claims.claim_summary: Norm clipping benefits SeerAttention and FlexPrefill-Llama, while norm balancing helps FlexPrefill

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 8 shows lower attention-output error in every evaluated framework–backbone pair, with all four reported paired confidence intervals above zero.
claims.claim_summary: MASA significantly reduces attention-output approximation error across all tested model frameworks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The relative reductions are 0.41% for MInference, 2.10% for SeerAttention, and 2.34% and 7.17% for FlexPrefill on Llama and Qwen, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: MASA reduces attention output approximation error by 0.41% to 7.17% across baselines

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The evaluated MASA configurations produce outputs closer to dense attention, providing empirical support for the matrix-approximation view alongside the downstream accuracy results.
claims.claim_summary: MASA brings sparse attention outputs closer to dense attention across evaluated configurations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We argue that this is the core conceptual issue: sparse attention should be formulated as matrix approximation, not as blindly choosing the largest values from a bag of entries.
claims.claim_summary: We argue that this is the core conceptual issue: sparse attention should be formulated as matrix approximation, not as blindly choosing the largest values from a bag of entries.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Based on this view, we propose Matrix Approximation Sparse Attention (MASA).
